newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: CA says has no idea about Bank Austria's plans.
newsitem.headline: CA says has no idea about Bank Austria's plans.

text.p: Austria's flagship bank Creditanstalt said on Sunday it had not yet been informed about the plans and strategies of its new owner, former arch-rival Bank Austria.

"The plans and the strategy of Bank Austria are not yet known to us," a spokesman told Reuters, adding that he could not even confirm that Creditanstalt had officially been informed at all about its new majority shareholder.
"There will be no statement from us today," he said.

Market leader Bank Austria on Sunday was awarded the state's 70 percent voting stake in its main competitor and wants to buy out the remaining 30 percent of voting rights at a small premium to their current market value.

Creditanstalt's management, along with Austria's conservatives, has long balked at the prospect of falling under the control of Bank Austria, which is effectively controlled by the Social Democrat-led City of Vienna council.
As part of a coalition agreement between Social Democrats and the conservative People's Party, Bank Austria will be taken out of public control successively over the next seven years.
According to the deal, Creditanstalt will remain an independent bank for at least five years.

Bank Austria was expected to outline its plans for the former banker to the Austro-Hungarian empire at a news conference scheduled for 1 p.m. (1200 GMT) on Sunday. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
